done_when: forge land and forge close notice when the item's forge.toml pins a different release after a worker round and run the rest of the step under the newly pinned release, saying so in one line, instead of failing on settings the old release doesn't know; a command test covers a land started on an earlier release whose worker merges an upgraded default branch, for a repo adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: The revised Done-when explicitly includes commands' own default-branch merges, broadening the earlier worker-only requirement. This handoff still occurs after `_merge_default` returns. When an upgrade merges forge.toml cleanly but conflicts in generated guidance, `_merge_default` runs `forge sync` at src/forge/close.py:451 before returning. That subprocess uses the old release, whose `check_pin` validates the entire configuration at src/forge/repo.py:514 before selecting another release. A newly introduced key therefore stops both standalone close and land's close path, leaving the merge unfinished without reaching this handoff. Run conflict-resolution sync under the newly pinned release, finish the merge, then resume the original command.
findings.title: Not done: land and close switch releases before resolving generated merge conflicts

findings.body: The revised Done-when explicitly requires a land command test where land itself merges the upgraded default branch in an earlier-adopted repo. The matrix covers only land-build, land-fix and close-merge: both land cases make the worker merge the upgrade, while the own-merge case invokes standalone close (lines 96–105). Tests 2 and 3 likewise cover a worker merge and standalone close. Consequently, a regression that resumes close's merge as `forge close` instead of the original `forge land` could pass every added case while dropping land's remaining workflow. Extend the command matrix with the promised land-owned merge, including earlier adoption, and assert the release notice, continuation and completion.
findings.title: Not done: command proof for land's own upgrade merge in an earlier-adopted repo

why: When a running forge land or close started under one pinned Forge release and the branch's forge.toml changes its pin mid-run (a worker merges the default branch after an upgrade), the old release keeps running and fails on the new forge.toml ('fast_test is not a forge.toml key'), stopping the item (reported by a client session on v1.2.8)
